original_value:
Large-scale binder jetting provides a promising alternative to manual sculpting of sandstone. The weak build material, however, severely limits its use in architectural ornamentation. We propose a structural optimization that jointly optimizes an ornament's strength-to-weight ratio and balance under self-weight, thermal, wind, and live loads. To account for the difference in the tensile and compressive strength of the build material, we turn the Bresler-Pister criterion into a failure potential, measuring the distance to failure. Integrated into an XFEM-based level set formulation, we minimize this potential by changing the topology and shape of the internal structure. To deal with uncertainties in the location of live loads, and the direction of wind loads, we first estimate loads that lead to the weakest structure, then minimize the potential of failure under identified worst-case loads. With the help of first-order optimality constraints, we unify our worst-case load estimation and structural optimization into a
            continuous
            optimization. We demonstrate applications in art, furniture design, and architectural ornamentation with three large-scale 3D printed examples.

result.paraphrase: Large-scale binder jetting is a promising substitute for manual sandstone sculpting, but the weak build material greatly restricts its use in architectural ornament. We present a structural optimization method that simultaneously improves an ornament’s strength-to-weight ratio and its stability under self-weight, thermal, wind, and live loads. Because the build material has different tensile and compressive strengths, we reformulate the Bresler-Pister criterion as a failure potential that measures distance to failure. Embedded in an XFEM-based level set framework, this potential is reduced by altering the topology and shape of the internal structure. To handle uncertainty in live-load placement and wind direction, we first identify loads that produce the weakest structure and then minimize failure potential under those worst-case loads. Using first-order optimality constraints, we combine worst-case load estimation and structural optimization into one continuous optimization problem. We show applications in art, furniture design, and architectural ornamentation through three large-scale 3D-printed examples.
